package iac // import "github.com/geoffmilleraz/fathom/pkg/lang/iac"

Package iac reads what an infrastructure-as-code file declares: each resource,
data source or module call, and each attribute it sets, with a path,
a value class and a span. It is part of fathom's language library (ADR-092,
docs/design/lang-library.md section 5) and, like pkg/lang, needs no store,
daemon, index, git or network.

A read never runs init, a plan, a provider or a program, and never expands
a module. It reads Terraform and OpenTofu (.tf, .tofu, and a directory as
one module), CloudFormation and SAM templates (YAML or JSON) and Pulumi YAML
programs.

# Classes, not values

Every attribute reads as one of five classes: literal (written as a constant),
defaulted (resolves only through a variable default or a local chain ending
in one), reference (names another resource, data source, module output or
parameter), expression (computed, with no static answer) or unknown (the reader
could not classify it). Absence is not a class: "this attribute is unset" comes
from comparing a read with a contract.

Attr.Value is empty unless the caller passes WithValues. Even then the reader
withholds what its source marks secret (a sensitive or ephemeral Terraform
variable's default, a CloudFormation NoEcho parameter, a Pulumi secret and
fn::secret), and the caller still learns that a literal or default is there.

# The read guarantee

ReadFile and ReadModule return by a deadline, DefaultReadDeadline, which
WithDeadline may lower and nothing raises. Go cannot interrupt a goroutine, so a
read that overruns is abandoned, not stopped: it keeps its CPU until it returns
on its own and its result is discarded. Once GOMAXPROCS abandoned reads are
still running, a read starts nothing and returns ErrBusy. A caller reading input
it does not trust reads through a process it can kill: `fathom-lang resources`
does, by default.

Output is deterministic. Every slice is non-nil and sorted, and equal inputs
give byte-equal JSON.

CONSTANTS

const (
	ToolTerraform      = "terraform"
	ToolCloudFormation = "cloudformation"
	ToolPulumi         = "pulumi"
)
    Tool values of Resource.Tool.

const (
	ModeManaged   = "managed"
	ModeData      = "data"
	ModeModule    = "module"
	ModeEphemeral = "ephemeral"
)
    Mode values of Resource.Mode. A module call is a resource-like relation and
    is never expanded.

const DefaultReadDeadline = 30 * time.Second
    DefaultReadDeadline is how long ReadFile and ReadModule wait for one read:
    30 seconds, the same bound as lang.DefaultReadDeadline. WithDeadline may
    lower it, never raise it. The value is a literal; TestPublicConstantValues
    holds it to pkg/lang's.

const MaxFileBytes = 2 * 1024 * 1024
    MaxFileBytes is the largest file a read accepts, the product's own limit
    of 2 MiB. A larger file is refused whole with ErrLimit. A directory read
    accepts 64 MiB across its files and 4,096 files. The value is a literal;
    TestPublicConstantValues holds it.


VARIABLES

var ErrBusy = errors.New("read-busy: reads that passed their deadline are still running, so this read was not started")
    ErrBusy is returned, with nothing read, when GOMAXPROCS reads that passed
    their deadline are still running. It clears as they finish.

var ErrDeadline = errors.New("read-deadline: the read passed its deadline and was abandoned, so none of its facts are returned")
    ErrDeadline is returned by a read that passed its deadline. The reader is
    abandoned, not stopped, and none of its facts are returned.

var ErrLimit = iacfacts.ErrLimit
    ErrLimit is wrapped by every refusal at a limit: a file or directory over
    its size, more attributes than a read holds, a value past its bound.
    The message names the limit and a count, never source text.

var ErrNotFound = errors.New("iac catalog: not found")
    ErrNotFound matches (errors.Is) a lookup the catalog cannot answer:
    a version it does not hold, a type it does not list or a provider it was not
    built for.


TYPES

type Attr struct {
	// Path is versioning[*].enabled or rule[*].id: every nested Terraform block segment takes [*], one block or
	// several, and so does every CloudFormation or Pulumi list element. A resource's own lifecycle block is
	// meta-configuration and takes none. The path is empty for the one attribute at the root that stands for a
	// Properties value the reader could not walk (an intrinsic, an alias, an interpolation); it reads unknown.
	Path  string `json:"path"`
	Class Class  `json:"class"`
	// Value is set only under WithValues, and only for literal and defaulted classes whose value could be
	// computed without evaluating a function, and never for what the source marks secret. A number is an int64
	// when it is an integer in range written without a fraction or exponent, a float64 when float64 holds it
	// exactly, a json.Number with its exact text when it is finite as float64 and does not fit either, and its
	// source text as a string when it is past float64's range. json.Marshal of a Value never fails.
	Value any `json:"value,omitempty"`
	// Refs are the static references the value reads, sorted: var.x, aws_s3_bucket.logs.id, Param, Res.Arn.
	// They name things, never values.
	Refs []string `json:"refs"`
	Span Span     `json:"span"`
}
    Attr is one attribute of a resource.

type Catalog struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Catalog is a provider contract catalog an operator placed on disk
    (docs/design/iac-facts.md section 4): a deterministic zip of one provider's
    major line, holding every stable release's resource, data source and
    ephemeral resource schemas as names, types and flags. OpenCatalog validates
    its manifest and keeps nothing else: each lookup opens the zip, reads one
    version index and one blob, and closes it. A Catalog holds no file handle
    and no memo, is safe for concurrent use, and is never closed.

    The library fetches nothing. A catalog is built by the operator from a local
    schema export, with their own tools.

func OpenCatalog(path string) (*Catalog, error)
    OpenCatalog opens the catalog at path and validates its manifest:
    the format, the kind, a provider source and major line, and a version list
    that is valid, ascending and inside the line. A catalog over its size or
    entry bound, or with a corrupt manifest, is refused with a *CatalogError.
    Opening reads no schema.

func (c *Catalog) Contract(source, version, typ string) (*Contract, error)
    Contract returns the type's contract at an exact version. The type is looked
    up as a resource, then as a data source, then as an ephemeral resource,
    and Contract.Kind says which answered: a type that is both a resource and
    a data source reads as the resource, and KindContract asks for the other.
    It opens the catalog, reads one version index and one blob, and closes it.

    source is the provider address, which must be the catalog's (lower case;
    no host is the default registry, and the two default registries stand in
    for each other). version must be one of Versions: a nearest version is
    never answered. A type or version the catalog lacks is a *CatalogError that
    matches ErrNotFound.

func (c *Catalog) KindContract(source, version string, kind Kind, typ string) (*Contract, error)
    KindContract is Contract for one kind.

func (c *Catalog) Line() string
    Line is the provider's major version: one catalog holds every release of one
    line.

func (c *Catalog) ReplacementFacts() string
    ReplacementFacts is the catalog's own claim about replacement facts:
    "absent" for a catalog that carries none.

func (c *Catalog) Source() string
    Source is the provider address the catalog was built for, host included.

func (c *Catalog) Versions() []string
    Versions lists the releases the catalog holds, oldest first.

type CatalogError struct {
	Scope  string
	Code   string
	Reason string
}
    CatalogError is a catalog or one answer that a bound or a check refused.
    Code is one of catalog-bytes, entries, manifest-bytes, index-bytes,
    blob-bytes, depth, fact-bytes, corrupt, format or not-found, and Scope is
    "catalog" when the whole catalog is refused and "answer" when one lookup is.
    Reason is a sentence a caller can print and holds no schema text.

func (e *CatalogError) Error() string

func (e *CatalogError) Is(target error) bool
    Is reports a not-found error as ErrNotFound.

type Class string
    Class is how an attribute's value is known.

const (
	// ClassLiteral: written as a constant. A check may treat it as a fact.
	ClassLiteral Class = "literal"
	// ClassDefaulted: resolves only through a variable default or a local chain ending in one. A check may treat
	// it as an assumption an operator can override.
	ClassDefaulted Class = "defaulted"
	// ClassReference: names another resource, data source, module output or parameter. A check may treat it as a
	// relation.
	ClassReference Class = "reference"
	// ClassExpression: computed, with no static answer. A check treats it as unknown.
	ClassExpression Class = "expression"
	// ClassUnknown: the reader could not classify it. A check treats it as unknown.
	ClassUnknown Class = "unknown"
)
    The five classes. Absence is not one.

type Contract struct {
	Catalog string `json:"catalog"`
	Source  string `json:"source"`
	Version string `json:"version"`
	Kind    Kind   `json:"kind"`
	Type    string `json:"type"`
	// Digest is the sha256 of the schema blob.
	Digest string `json:"digest"`
	// ReplacementFacts is the catalog's claim about replacement facts ("absent" when it carries none).
	ReplacementFacts string         `json:"replacement_facts"`
	Attributes       []ContractAttr `json:"attributes"`
}
    Contract is what a catalog states about one type at one version. Every fact
    cites the catalog, the version and the digest of the blob it was read from.

type ContractAttr struct {
	// Path spells a nested block with [*], as the resource reads do: versioning[*].enabled. A block's own entry is
	// versioning[*]. An attribute with nested attributes spells list and set nesting with [*] and the rest with a dot.
	Path string `json:"path"`
	// Block is true for a nested block, whose own entry carries MinItems and MaxItems.
	Block bool `json:"block"`
	// Type is the attribute's type as the schema export writes it ("string", or JSON such as ["list","string"]),
	// "nested_type" for an attribute that holds nested attributes, and "" for a block.
	Type string `json:"type"`
	// Required and Optional state whether a user must or may set the attribute. Both false with Computed true is an
	// attribute only the provider sets. Both false with Computed false means the catalog states neither: a
	// CloudFormation nested entry whose object the importer could not resolve. Read that as unknown, never as optional
	// or as unrequired. A block entry states MinItems and MaxItems instead.
	Required   bool `json:"required"`
	Optional   bool `json:"optional"`
	Computed   bool `json:"computed"`
	Sensitive  bool `json:"sensitive"`
	WriteOnly  bool `json:"write_only"`
	Deprecated bool `json:"deprecated"`
	MinItems   int  `json:"min_items"`
	MaxItems   int  `json:"max_items"`
	// Replacement is nil when the catalog states none for this attribute.
	Replacement *Replacement `json:"replacement"`
	// JSONPath is where in the type's schema blob the entry was read, dot-joined, so a reader can check it.
	JSONPath string `json:"json_path"`
}
    ContractAttr is one attribute or nested block of a type's contract.

type Dropped struct {
	Name string `json:"name"`
}
    Dropped names a resource-section entry that was not read as a resource:
    a Fn::ForEach, an alias, a merge-only entry, a value that is not a mapping,
    an entry without a type, or a Terraform data source inside a check block
    (check.NAME.data.TYPE.NAME). Absence is never silent: a resource that is in
    neither Resources nor Dropped does not exist in the file.

type Export struct {
	Version string
	Path    string
}
    Export is one `tofu providers schema -json` file and the provider version
    the operator asserts it was made at. The version is recorded as given and is
    not checked against the export.

type ImportRequest struct {
	// Dir is the directory the catalog is installed in, created when it is missing. A catalog's file name comes from
	// its manifest, so one provider line, or one CloudFormation region, has one file in Dir.
	Dir string
	// Exports are the exports of ONE provider and one major line, one per release. A multi-provider export is
	// refused. Make one in a scratch directory whose configuration requires only that provider:
	// `tofu init && tofu providers schema -json > export.json`.
	Exports []Export
	// SchemaZip is a CloudFormation registry schema zip the operator fetched, Region the region it is for
	// (us-east-1). A region holds one snapshot, so a new zip replaces the region's catalog.
	SchemaZip string
	Region    string
	// Licence is the SPDX identifier recorded in the manifest, and Tool names the tool that made the exports.
	Licence string
	Tool    string
	// Replace swaps a release the installed catalog holds with different content. Without it that is refused. It
	// does not apply to a schema zip.
	Replace bool
}
    ImportRequest names what to build a catalog from and where to install it.
    Exactly one input is set: Exports, or SchemaZip with Region. Every path is a
    local file, and nothing is downloaded.

type ImportResult struct {
	// Path is the installed file, Name its file name, SHA256 its digest and Bytes its size. Source is the provider
	// address (aws/cloudformation for a schema zip), Line the provider's major version or the region, and Versions the
	// releases it holds, oldest first (one sha256-<12 hex> snapshot label for a schema zip).
	Path, Name, SHA256 string
	Bytes              int64
	Source, Line       string
	Versions           []string
	// ReplacementFacts is the manifest's own claim: "absent" for a catalog built from exports, which carries facts
	// 1 to 4 and 7 and no replacement facts, and "contract" for a schema zip, whose replacement facts are the
	// schema's createOnlyProperties and conditionalCreateOnlyProperties.
	ReplacementFacts string
	// Facts says in a sentence what the catalog carries.
	Facts string

	// Exports only. Merged is true when a catalog of the same provider line was installed and its releases were
	// kept. Added are the releases the import brought, Kept the installed releases it did not name, Unchanged the
	// named releases whose content equals the installed one and Replaced the ones Replace swapped. All are in
	// version order.
	Merged                           bool
	Added, Kept, Unchanged, Replaced []string

	// Schema zip only. Types is the resource types read, SchemaDigest the sha256 over the zip's entry names and
	// bodies (its embedded build time is ignored) and Date the day the zip was built. SnapshotReplaced is true when
	// the region already had a catalog, PreviousDigest is that catalog's digest and SnapshotUnchanged is true when
	// it equals the new one.
	Types              int
	SchemaDigest, Date string
	SnapshotReplaced   bool
	PreviousDigest     string
	SnapshotUnchanged  bool
}
    ImportResult is the catalog an import installed.

func ImportCatalog(req ImportRequest) (*ImportResult, error)
    ImportCatalog builds a provider contract catalog from local files and
    installs it in req.Dir. It is the builder `fathom iac import` uses,
    so a library consumer needs no fathom binary: a `tofu providers schema
    -json` export becomes a catalog with attributes, required, sensitive,
    deprecated and upgrade-impact facts and no replacement facts, and says so
    in its manifest; a CloudFormation registry schema zip becomes a region's
    catalog whose replacement facts are the schemas' own. Open the result with
    OpenCatalog(res.Path).

    An import into a directory that already holds the same provider line merges:
    every release held stays, the named ones are added, and the result lists
    what was added, kept, unchanged and replaced. Nothing is installed when
    anything is refused. A refusal of a bound or a check is a *CatalogError;
    a bad request or an unreadable file is a plain error. ImportCatalog reads
    and writes only the paths in req.

type Kind string
    Kind names the section of a catalog a type is looked up in.

const (
	KindResource   Kind = "resource"
	KindDataSource Kind = "data_source"
	KindEphemeral  Kind = "ephemeral_resource"
)
    The kinds a catalog holds.

type Multiplicity struct {
	Kind  MultiplicityKind `json:"kind"`
	Class Class            `json:"class"`
	Refs  []string         `json:"refs"`
	Span  Span             `json:"span"`
}
    Multiplicity is the instance count of a resource. Class is the class of
    the count, for_each or condition expression, and is "" for MultiSingle.
    Refs names what the expression reads.

type MultiplicityKind string
    MultiplicityKind is how many instances a resource declares.

const (
	MultiSingle    MultiplicityKind = "single"
	MultiCount     MultiplicityKind = "count"
	MultiForEach   MultiplicityKind = "for_each"
	MultiCondition MultiplicityKind = "condition"
)
    The kinds of Multiplicity.Kind.

type NoReaderError struct {
	// Path is the path the caller gave.
	Path string
}
    NoReaderError is the error of a file that no reader here reads.

func (e *NoReaderError) Error() string

type Option func(*config) error
    Option configures a read.

func WithDeadline(d time.Duration) Option
    WithDeadline lowers the time a read may take. A deadline above
    DefaultReadDeadline, or one that is not positive, is an error: no option
    raises the bound.

func WithValues() Option
    WithValues keeps Attr.Value, which is empty without it. It is the only way a
    value is returned. The reader still withholds what its source marks secret,
    and refuses an input whose values pass its bounds.

type Replacement struct {
	// Class is "replace", "conditional" or "unknown".
	Class string `json:"class"`
	// Provenance names the provider source the fact was read from.
	Provenance string `json:"provenance"`
}
    Replacement is one attribute's replacement fact: what changing it does to
    the resource, and where the claim came from. A catalog carries replacement
    facts only when its manifest says so (Catalog.ReplacementFacts is not
    "absent"), and an answer never says a change is safe: it says what the
    contract states.

type Resource struct {
	// Tool is a Tool* value, and Mode a Mode* value.
	Tool string `json:"tool"`
	Mode string `json:"mode"`
	// Type is aws_s3_bucket, AWS::S3::Bucket or aws:s3/bucket:Bucket.
	Type string `json:"type"`
	Name string `json:"name"`
	// Provider is the provider selection a Terraform resource states (aws.west), and "" for the rest.
	Provider     string       `json:"provider"`
	Span         Span         `json:"span"`
	Attrs        []Attr       `json:"attrs"`
	Multiplicity Multiplicity `json:"multiplicity"`
}
    Resource is one resource, data source or module call.

type ResourceSet struct {
	Resources []Resource `json:"resources"`
	// SyntaxErrors counts the syntax errors the parser reported, keys a mapping repeats, YAML documents after the
	// first (which are not read), values the reader could not walk, a resource section that is not a mapping and a
	// resource whose merge key may carry its properties. A read still returns the resources it could parse, and an
	// attribute it could not read is unknown, never what a parser's recovery guessed.
	SyntaxErrors int       `json:"syntax_errors"`
	Dropped      []Dropped `json:"dropped"`
}
    ResourceSet is what one read returned. Resources are sorted by span and
    attributes by path, then span.

func ReadFile(ctx context.Context, filePath string, src []byte, opts ...Option) (*ResourceSet, error)
    ReadFile reads one file's resources. The reader is chosen by the path and,
    for a YAML or JSON template, by the content: .tf and .tofu read as Terraform
    or OpenTofu, .tf.json and .tofu.json as its JSON syntax (which is not read:
    the result holds no resource and one syntax error), Pulumi.yaml as Pulumi
    YAML, and any other .yaml, .yml, .json or .template file that reads as
    a CloudFormation template as CloudFormation. Any other file returns a
    *NoReaderError.

    Path is only a name and a classifier: nothing is read from disk, and it is
    the File of every Span. src is not modified. A file past MaxFileBytes is
    refused with ErrLimit. The read returns by DefaultReadDeadline (lowered by
    WithDeadline) with ErrDeadline, and with ErrBusy while GOMAXPROCS abandoned
    reads are running. A context that ends first returns its error and abandons
    the read the same way.

    An error never carries a value from the file.

func ReadModule(ctx context.Context, fsys fs.FS, dir string, opts ...Option) (*ResourceSet, error)
    ReadModule reads one Terraform or OpenTofu directory of fsys as a module:
    every .tf and .tofu file directly in dir, with variable defaults
    and locals resolved across them, so an attribute that reads var.x,
    or a local chain ending in a variable default, is defaulted. It follows
    OpenTofu's file rules: a .tofu file shadows the .tf file of the same name,
    an override file adds no resource and marks what it names unknown, dot files
    and editor backups are skipped. A module call reads as a relation and is
    never expanded, and no other directory is listed. Spans name the files as
    dir joined with the file name.

    dir is an fs.ValidPath ("." for the root of fsys). The directory is refused
    with ErrLimit past 4,096 files, 2 MiB a file or 64 MiB in all. The deadline,
    busy and context rules are ReadFile's.

type Span struct {
	File      string `json:"file"`
	StartLine int    `json:"start_line"`
	StartCol  int    `json:"start_col"`
	EndLine   int    `json:"end_line"`
	EndCol    int    `json:"end_col"`
}
    Span is a region of a source file. Lines and columns are 1-based, columns
    count characters and not bytes, and the end is exclusive. File is the path
    the caller gave.
